question: Should OpenClaw publish a signed standalone Android APK outside Google Play, and if so through which official channel and signing/provenance policy?
rationale: Current main can archive a signed third-party APK, but publishing it changes the trusted Android distribution surface and cannot be decided safely by an automated fix PR.

options.title: Publish signed APK via existing lane
options.body: Reuse the current Android archive and signing tooling, add maintainer-approved publication plus checksums/provenance, and document the supported install path.

options.title: Keep Google Play only
options.body: Explicitly decide that standalone APK and F-Droid distribution are unsupported for now, then update docs to warn users toward Google Play or source builds only.

options.title: Choose another official channel first
options.body: Adopt F-Droid or another non-Play channel, then implement release automation around that channel's review, signing, and provenance requirements.

recommendation.title: Publish signed APK via existing lane
recommendation.body: Reuse the current Android archive and signing tooling, add maintainer-approved publication plus checksums/provenance, and document the supported install path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current archive, signing, Play upload, and mobile release ref history makes this the closest available routing owner for the release-path decision.
